recipes.title: Add a project feature
steps: Name the feature's authoritative state, behavior, scene bridge, and external dependencies.
Place the feature in one declared project module outside addons/gf.
Use a GF Model, System, Utility, or Controller only for the responsibility it owns.
Register long-lived architecture members from the composition root; keep scene objects scene-owned.
Test observable state transitions and lifecycle cleanup.
avoid: One class per architecture role without responsibility
Business fields added to GF resources
Scene nodes retained by long-lived services

recipes.title: Compose project modules and adapters
steps: Create a project-owned GFInstaller as the composition root.
Select concrete services and provider adapters from contract constraints.
Register stable protocols before dependent systems initialize.
Keep feature flow and SDK callbacks out of the installer.
Verify initialization, disposal, and replacement in tests.
avoid: Service locator calls scattered through domain code
Platform checks spread across systems

recipes.title: Implement an owned async operation
steps: Choose the node, service, or request that owns the operation.
Define success, failure, cancellation, and timeout terminal states.
Bind cancellation to owner disposal or scene exit.
Normalize callbacks or signals into one completion boundary.
Observe every terminal state and test late callbacks.
avoid: Fire-and-forget work with hidden failure
Awaiting a signal whose emitter can disappear

recipes.title: Load a resource with explicit ownership
steps: Resolve a stable resource key or catalog entry instead of scattering paths.
Acquire through GFAssetUtility with an owner, group, or explicit release policy.
Handle cancellation and load failure before exposing the resource.
Release the handle when the owner ends.
Test cache and owner-disposal behavior.
avoid: Unowned long-lived cache pins
Runtime content identity based only on raw res:// paths

recipes.title: Compile project configuration
steps: Keep business schema in project-owned source and schema files.
Use Reader, Layout, Validation, Target, and Commit stages as separate concerns.
Inspect the versioned IR before materialization when adding custom targets.
Fail closed on duplicate identities, invalid references, and partial commits.
Verify freshness fingerprints and rollback.
avoid: Project columns hardcoded into GF stages
Writing outputs before all semantic validation passes

recipes.title: Track versioned analytics through a dedicated outbox
steps: Define one stable event name and a schema version in the exact 1..2_147_483_647 range with a strict GFDictionarySchema over caller-supplied properties only.
Register the exact GFAnalyticsEventSchema before producers call track_versioned, and treat missing or invalid versions as rejected events.
Add a new explicit schema version for contract changes; do not silently migrate, reinterpret, or select the latest version.
Create a dedicated GFRequestOutboxUtility with its own storage path, retention, replay filter, transport callback, and account or consent lifecycle.
Configure GFAnalyticsOutboxAdapter and attach enqueue_payload as the analytics transport callback; this adapter accepts a batch only after enqueue_with_report reports durable persistence.
Treat delivery as at-least-once, forward the stable idempotency key, and require the server to validate schema, identity, authorization, size, and duplicates.
Test invalid properties, unknown versions, persistence failure, restart recovery, duplicate delivery, account changes, consent withdrawal, and expired authentication.
avoid: PII collection inferred from a valid schema
Analytics sharing an outbox with purchases or cloud saves
Schema versions treated as authentication or migration permission
Exactly-once claims without receiver-side idempotency

recipes.title: Define persistence and save ownership
steps: Declare persistence mode and compatibility guarantees in the project contract.
Choose local dictionary storage or scene save graph by ownership shape.
Assign stable identities and project-owned serializers or data sources.
Make migrations explicit and transactional.
Test corruption, interruption, old versions, and missing entities.
avoid: Persisting process-local IDs
Treating encryption, integrity, and obfuscation as equivalent

recipes.title: Coordinate a transactional save profile
steps: Define one stable section provider per independently owned data boundary and keep section payloads business-owned.
Register the profile, providers, complete migration chain, recovery policy, and explicit storage backend before the first operation.
Observe the typed operation result for success, validation failure, cancellation, rollback failure, and recovery outcome.
Use generation coalescing for repeated requests and a flush barrier before shutdown, account switch, or destructive navigation.
Fault-inject interrupted writes, corrupt and future versions, provider failure, migration gaps, rollback failure, and late completion.
avoid: Resetting every failed load to an empty save
Providers mutating another section during capture or restore
Fire-and-forget save calls during owner disposal

recipes.title: Adapt a platform lobby provider
steps: Declare provider-neutral contract methods, request/result schemas, byte budgets, capability requirements, concurrency, cancellation support, and sensitive fields.
Keep Steam, Epic, console, or service SDK calls inside the adapter.
Map every lobby call to a GFNetworkLobbyOperationHandle by request ID and normalize initialization, cancellation, timeout, provider shutdown, and late callbacks.
Publish launch and invite callbacks as deduplicated GFPlatformActivationIntent records; adopt provider MultiplayerPeer instances with explicit owned or borrowed lifecycle.
Run GFPlatformAdapterConformance and fault-inject unavailable SDK, invalid schemas, concurrency, cancellation, timeout, duplicate terminal callbacks, disconnect, and ownership transfer.
Let project code own lobby visibility, matchmaking, authority, UI, product policy, and fallback.
avoid: Provider IDs leaking into portable domain models
Uncorrelated callback-only completion
A GFSteamManager-style global business facade

recipes.title: Adapt cloud or platform storage
steps: Implement provider calls behind GFStorageBackend or a project-owned equivalent.
Normalize keys, revisions, availability, errors, and cancellation.
Declare conflict and offline policy in project code.
Keep credentials and account data outside logs and feedback drafts.
Test stale revisions, partial failures, quota, offline recovery, and retries.
avoid: Cloud policy embedded in generic storage
Last-write-wins without an explicit project decision

recipes.title: Implement a replaceable provider backend
steps: Select the narrow GF protocol that matches the provider capability.
Declare capability support before handling requests.
Translate provider errors and lifecycle into stable project-facing results.
Fallback only when project policy explicitly permits it.
Contract-test the backend independently from the SDK-facing wrapper.
avoid: Provider-specific methods added to a generic protocol
Silent fallback that changes product behavior

recipes.title: Implement a network transport backend
steps: Keep transport bytes and connection state separate from project messages.
Declare authority, reliability, ordering, and payload limits in project contracts.
Normalize peer identity, disconnect reasons, optional metrics, and MultiplayerPeer ownership at the adapter boundary.
Use GF network contracts for stable payloads when appropriate.
Test loss, duplication, reordering, reconnect, oversized payloads, and shutdown.
avoid: Transport callbacks mutating gameplay state directly
Assuming a transport implies authority policy

recipes.title: Coordinate bounded authoritative snapshots
steps: Keep a finite raw packet limit and peer-binding validator in GFNetworkUtility, and pass its actual source peer to the coordinator.
Create a trusted unique epoch, configure explicit local and authority peers, and register each authorized replica from project session policy.

Implement a synchronous project adapter with strict state and input schemas, side-effect-free validation, and entity control checks based on actual_peer_id at enqueue and again at the target authority tick.
Submit recipient-bound inputs, advance one authority or prediction tick at a time, and send only the latest coordinator-issued full snapshot to each recipient.
Handle resync and permanent fault terminals explicitly, rebuild adapter state before a new epoch, and test spoofing, replay, stale packets, budget exhaustion, rollback failure, and callback reentry.
avoid: Authority inferred from payload or lobby metadata
Automatic scene-tree or entity replication
Inbound delta or patch without a versioned baseline protocol
Unbounded history, pending input, replay, or packet limits
Awaiting, networking, or state mutation inside adapter validation hooks

recipes.title: Escalate a project finding to GF
steps: Minimize the failure outside project business flow.
Classify project misuse, framework defect, documentation gap, reusable mechanism, or adapter gap.
Create a structured candidate with expected, actual, reproduction, environment, impact, and workaround.
Generate a redacted draft and inspect the exact payload.
Check duplicates and submit only after explicit approval of the payload hash.
avoid: Uploading raw project files or logs
Submitting speculative ideas as confirmed defects

recipes.title: Organize optional project content
steps: Query packages through provider-neutral criteria and keep entitlement, download, activation, and CDN decisions in project services.
Translate eligible package records into owner-scoped asset catalog providers without leaking physical roots into gameplay code.
Mount providers into GFAssetCatalogRuntime with explicit owner, priority, collision policy, and teardown.
Resolve stable resource keys from the runtime catalog before acquiring assets through the normal asset ownership lifecycle.
Test missing content, duplicate keys, priority ties, provider removal, stale mounts, dependency cycles, and owner disposal.
avoid: Download URLs embedded in runtime content records
Gameplay rules keyed to physical file paths
Global mounts without a lifecycle owner

recipes.title: Add input contexts and rebinding
steps: Define project-owned abstract actions and contexts.
Map device events through bindings, modifiers, and triggers.
Use a detector and conflict analysis before committing rebinds.
Persist project rebind policy separately from gameplay state.
Test context overlap, device changes, cancellation, and inaccessible bindings.
avoid: Gameplay code reading physical keys directly
A rebinding UI silently resolving conflicts

recipes.title: Compose a UI screen flow
steps: Separate logical navigation layers from CanvasLayer drawing order.
Represent screen intent in project-owned navigation requests and state.
Bind controls to reactive state without placing business decisions in views.
Define modal, replace, hide-under, focus, back behavior, and adjacent preload candidates explicitly.
Observe typed route operation results and test rapid transitions, preload failure, cancellation, scene disposal, focus restoration, and duplicate requests.
avoid: Cross-layer cleanup assumed from replace
Global UI state embedded in individual controls

recipes.title: Execute an asynchronous UI route transition
steps: Resolve the route and build its bounded preload plan before mutating the visible stack.
Choose an explicit preload policy and preserve the current screen until route commit is possible.
Await the route operation and branch on its typed terminal result instead of inferring success from signals or node presence.
Let the project navigation owner reject stale or superseded results, own focus and back policy, and release preloaded assets at its lifecycle boundary.
Test duplicate requests, stale completion, invalid routes, preload failure, transition failure, cancellation, and back-stack invariants.
avoid: Mutating the route stack before prerequisites succeed
Treating cancellation as success
Leaking preloaded handles across route ownership

recipes.title: Choose state machine, flow, or action queue
steps: Use a state machine for mutually exclusive durable modes.
Use a flow graph for inspectable progression through heterogeneous steps.
Use an action queue for ordered or parallel transient work, especially presentation.
Assign one owner for cancellation and terminal reporting.
Test interruption, loops, missing targets, and owner disposal.
avoid: Nesting orchestrators to model the same state
Using a visual queue as authoritative domain state

recipes.title: Publish bounded diagnostics
steps: Choose the minimum fields needed to answer a concrete operational question.
Publish stable cached facts directly and register expensive or freshness-sensitive facts as owner-bound lazy providers.
Evaluate providers only from explicit support or failure paths with request, duration, cardinality, depth, and text budgets.
Treat provider failures and reentrancy as isolated typed results rather than snapshot-wide failure.
Define retention, consent, redaction, and reserved section-name policy before collection.
Test disabled collection, owner disposal, timeout, reentrancy, oversized values, provider exceptions, and secret redaction.
avoid: Unbounded histories
Precise device, account, scene, or path data collected by default
Evaluating lazy providers in frame or polling loops

recipes.title: Capture a bounded diagnostic session trace
steps: Define a project-owned minimum event schema, explicit consent boundary, retention policy, and redaction profile before enabling a trace.
Apply one bounded recipe before the session starts, with finite channel, checkpoint, event, payload, text, depth, and byte budgets.
Record only stable channel events and request lazy diagnostic checkpoints at concrete failure or support moments.
Export a sanitized local report; keep upload, incident policy, and business recovery outside GFSessionTraceUtility.
Test disabled consent, budget exhaustion, invalid recipes, provider failure, redaction, repeated sessions, and teardown.
avoid: Always-on precise telemetry
Unbounded arbitrary Variant payloads
Embedding upload or gameplay recovery policy in the trace recipe

recipes.title: Expose a bounded runtime Agent endpoint
steps: Define the smallest project-owned synchronous operation and closed JSON request/response schemas; do not expose arbitrary reflection or generic command dispatch.
Register endpoints while the environment is disabled, then install project policy providers for business authorization or approval requirements.
Create the environment on a long-lived owner thread; make transport workers enforce pre-decode body and connection limits, then marshal every environment call back to the owner thread.
Enable the environment only after the outer transport is authenticated, and issue a short-lived session with exact endpoint grants and finite rate/replay budgets.
Before mutating the registry, a Provider, or external policy state in place, call invalidate_policy_context on the owner thread so every earlier credential is revoked.
Keep the bearer token out of the request envelope, logs, URLs, snapshots, and persistence; use a unique request ID for every authenticated attempt.
Observe typed results and payload-free audit events, revoke sessions on ownership changes, and disable or dispose the environment during teardown.

Test invalid credentials, expiry, replay, rate exhaustion, schema and byte budgets, policy denial, policy-context invalidation, cross-thread rejection, endpoint re-registration, callback revocation, and secret absence.
avoid: Calling the environment or mutating policy objects directly from transport workers
Generic reflection, file, shell, screenshot, or diagnostics bridges
Treating an in-process callback boundary as an OS sandbox
Persisting bearer tokens or copying business payloads into audit

recipes.title: Define a deterministic simulation scope
steps: Declare which inputs, state, ticks, and outputs must reproduce.
Use fixed GF random state and canonical supported value types.
Exclude or quantize nondeterministic physics, clocks, floats, and provider callbacks.
Record seeds and canonical state hashes.
Verify golden sequences across clean runs and target platforms.
avoid: Assuming Godot RNG implementation is a permanent wire contract
Hashing unordered or unsupported Variant graphs

recipes.title: Use a reusable domain component
steps: Select a component only for generic state and operations it already owns.
Keep item meaning, rewards, economy, balance, and progression policy in project systems.
Store project-specific fields in documented metadata or project-owned resources.
Define save and replication boundaries explicitly.
Test invalid IDs, limits, duplicate operations, and migration.
avoid: Subclassing generic data to hide an entire gameplay system
Adding one game's vocabulary to GF component code

recipes.title: Build a dialogue pipeline
steps: Compile strict project-owned source into GF dialogue resources at authoring time.
Provide condition, mutation, and text resolution callbacks from project context.
Keep UI, localization tables, characters, quests, and rewards outside the runner.
Persist stable line and response identities when resume is required.
Test missing targets, cycles, invalid mutations, cancellation, and source diagnostics.
avoid: Business mutation names hardcoded into the compiler
Dialogue UI owning authoritative quest state

recipes.title: Apply spatial or physics mechanisms
steps: Separate pure spatial math or sampling from world ownership and node mutation.
Declare coordinate, units, layer, update cadence, and authority contracts.
Use GFSpatialCanvas2D only to coordinate bounded view transforms, selection, and project-validated placement operation records.
Let the project choose candidates, validate placement, mutate TileMap or scene content, persist history or UGC, apply forces, and define collision policy.
Bound queries and incremental work.
Test empty worlds, invalid values, large coordinates, frame-rate variation, and disposal.
avoid: Physics ownership hidden inside a math helper
Treating GFSpatialCanvas2D as a TileMap editor, business-rule authority, save system, or UGC store
Unbounded world scans on frame callbacks
